newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hoechst share price will decide HMR issue.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst share price will decide HMR issue.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG will decide on any flotation of its Hoechst Marion Roussel (HMR) drugs unit based on whether the share price fully reflects the value of Hoechst, Hoechst's finance director said on Wednesday.

"As long as we feel that the...stock price of Hoechst AG does not adequately reflect the value of the group, the listing of HMR becomes an issue and we will make a decision going forward," Klaus Schmieder told a news conference in Paris.
HMR would be listed in Frankfurt, Paris and New York if it were floated, he added. Hoechst's buyout offer for Roussel Uclaf, announced earlier, may be part of that process.
The offer to buy Roussel minorities would create an HMR legal entity which would allow a flotation of HMR if Hoechst decided to go down that route, he said.
"The listing of HMR is an issue. We are contemplating doing that. We haven't made a decision yet. The first step in this process is to create the legal entity Hoechst Marion Roussel," he said.

"It (the flotation) will depend on a variety of factors, the most important being, do we need that to highlight the value of the Hoechst group. That is the key driver for our decision whether or not we take HMR public," he said.
Other key steps in Hoechst's strategy are to "carve out" its pharmaceuticals activities in Germany and then integrate those with HMR, Schmieder said.
"Then we will be looking at a global HMR legal entity which we will then be able to take to the stock exchange if we decide at that point to do so," he said.
The Roussel buy-out was not tied to Hoechst's announced plan to list its shares on the New York stock exchange, he said.
"There is no tie-in between our plan for that move...and this particular transaction," he said.

"This particular transaction is designed to maximise our opportunities in the pharmaceuticals areas and come up with a Hoechst Marion Roussel operation which is globally integrated and which can therefore better face the competition."
